numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Returned values had an incorrect array shape when the input had length-1 along an axis that was included in the `axis` keyword (e.g., produced `(5, 5)` instead of `(5, 1)`, and `(5, 5, 4)` instead of `(5, 1, 4)`). Also, for constant data with `axis` set to a tuple containing all axes, it returned `NaN` instead of the constant value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The returned array shape should match the expected reduction shape (e.g., `(5, 1)` or `(5, 1, 4)` respectively). For constant data with `axis` set to a tuple containing all axes, it should return the constant value (e.g., `1.0`) instead of `NaN`.
trigger_conditions: Input array has an axis length of 1 along any axis that is included in the `axis` keyword (shape/axis handling bug)
Constant input data with `axis` set to a tuple containing all axes

input_output_examples.source: pr_body:PR#16964 (axis tuple containing all axes, constant data)

oracle_clues: Change log states: wrong returned array shape would occur if input array had axis length of 1 along any axis not included in the axis keyword; and constant data with axis set to a tuple containing all axes returned NaN instead of constant value.
PR body explicitly states expected shapes and the constant expected value (`1.0`) instead of `NaN`.

category_specific_evidence: Fixed a bug in biweight_location, biweight_scale, and biweight_midvariance where the returned array shape would be wrong if the input array had an axis length of 1 along any axis that was not included in the axis keyword.
Also fixed a bug in these same functions where for constant data and axis set to a tuple containing all axes, the returned value would be NaN instead of the constant value.

PR#16964 example: for arr = np.ones((5, 1, 4, 10)) with axis=-1, val.shape was (5, 5) but should be (5, 1); for arr = np.ones((5, 1, 10)) with axis=-1, val.shape was (5, 5, 4) but should be (5, 1, 4).
PR#16964 example: for arr = np.ones((5, 1, 10)), biweight_location(arr, axis=(0, 1, 2)) returned np.float64(nan) but should be 1.0.
The commit message states: "Fix len-1 axis bug in biweight_midvariance and biweight_scale" and "Fix biweight stats for axis tuple containing all axes and constant data".
reproduction_risks: Reproduction depends on using biweight_location/biweight_scale/biweight_midvariance with an input that includes an axis of length 1 that is not part of the specified axis keyword (to trigger wrong output shape).
Reproduction depends on using constant data (all ones) and an axis tuple containing all axes to trigger NaN instead of the constant value.
